entries.notes: ERA5 reanalysis via the Open-Meteo archive endpoint, daily precipitation_sum for JJAS 06-01..09-30 in each year 2015-2025 (off-season days omitted because the fetch is rate-limited, not because they are unavailable) on a 0.5 degree grid (55.6 km), area-weighted over the existing Assam district polygons. Units are mm/day (daily totals). Published 2022 JJAS totals and the 2015-2025 JJAS mean per district. Class is reanalysis, never observed: ERA5 is a model-based reanalysis, not a gauge or satellite observation, and it is biased in complex terrain. It is sampled at 0.5 degree nodes (stride-2 of the native 0.25 degree grid) because the native request volume exceeds the free-tier rate limit; district areal means are therefore smoother than the native product, especially along the Himalayan and Barail margins.

entries.source_name: WorldPop 2020 population per 1 km cell (India, Aggregated)

entries.licence: Derived output; WorldPop CC BY 4.0 and terrain/channel licences as recorded
entries.notes: The only resident-count field is potentially_exposed_residents (the totals block repeats the peak-mask value as peak_mask_potentially_exposed_residents for reconciliation). It is class derived. Method: Static WorldPop 2020 population counts per 1 km cell. The peak-mask total uses the fractional 1 km cell area covered by the 90 m wet mask. District exposure is the zonal sum of population x wet fraction (cell-centre containment), so district values reconcile to the peak mask. district_population is the raw zonal population and exposed_share_of_district is the exposed share of it. Population totals are clipped to the AOI v2 core mask and published as population_within_aoi; the unclipped India-wide raster total is kept only under source.raster_total_unclipped with scope=India. Uncertainty: This is a static population raster crossed with a synthetic flood mask. It is not an impact assessment: it does not estimate humanitarian impact, population movement, or loss of life, and it carries no timing, warning or response information. WorldPop 2020 itself has model and census-input uncertainty, and a 1 km cell is coarse relative to the 90 m flood mask; treat the totals as order-of-magnitude planning context.
